preview.tournamentOverview: El Cardonal at Diamante is a new PGA Tour venue that rewards ball-striking and approach play over raw distance. The course's firm, fast conditions and strategic bunkering place a premium on accurate iron play and scrambling, making SG APP (20%) and SG Total (30%) the decisive factors.
preview.modelExplainer: Our model weights SG Total at 30% as the primary driver, followed by SG APP at 20% and SG OTT at 15%, reflecting the course's emphasis on approach play and tee-to-green control. SG PUT (15%) and SG ATG (10%) round out the skill-based metrics, while ancillary stats like Bogey Avoidance (4%) and Birdie/Bogey Ratio (3%) capture the importance of avoiding big numbers on a demanding layout. Driving Accuracy (3%) receives minimal weight, as the course's width and firm conditions reduce the penalty for missing fairways.
preview.pickApproach: We tier bets by combining tournamentRank with powerRank gaps, targeting players whose course-specific skills align with the 30% SG Total and 20% SG APP weights. We avoid players with negative SG APP marks unless offset by exceptional SG PUT or SG ATG performance that compensates for approach deficiencies.

article.title: World Wide Technology Championship: Model Targets Yellamaraju, Gerard, Lipsky at El Cardonal
article.dek: Sudarshan Yellamaraju leads the tournament model at 34 SG total while Ryan Gerard and David Lipsky rank second and third.
article.introduction: The tournament model ranks Sudarshan Yellamaraju first with 34 SG total, Ryan Gerard second at 94 SG total, and David Lipsky third at 89 SG total. All three players skipped the Scottish Open and carry zero tracked rounds in the major swing workload column. Their model ranks sit well ahead of their power ranks, creating the primary crossover signal for this 116-player field.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: The World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante carries a 116-player field and uses the supplied course weights: SG total 30%, SG approach 20%, SG off-the-tee 15%, SG putting 15%, SG around-the-green 10%, with smaller allocations to driving accuracy, bogey avoidance, and birdie/bogey ratio.

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: El Cardonal weights favor SG total and SG approach. Yellamaraju leads both with 34 SG total and 474 SG approach. Gerard posts the field's second-best SG approach at 712. Lipsky's 524 SG around-the-green and 485 SG putting add short-game stability under the 10% and 15% weights.

sections.heading: Model vs Power Rank Differential
sections.body: Yellamaraju's model rank of 1 sits 18 spots ahead of his power rank of 19. Gerard's model rank of 2 sits 29 spots ahead of his power rank of 31. Lipsky's model rank of 3 sits 21 spots ahead of his power rank of 24. These gaps constitute the main crossover signal.

sections.heading: Post-Open Workload and FedExCup Standing
sections.body: All three players show zero tracked rounds in the major swing workload column. Yellamaraju sits 58th in FedExCup, Gerard 17th, and Lipsky 85th. The zero-round workload and Scottish Open skip are recorded facts, not directional signals.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: Each player combines a top-10 model rank with a Scottish Open skip and zero tracked major-swing rounds. Yellamaraju, Gerard, and Lipsky all meet the supplied crossover definition of top-10 model rank ahead of power rank plus the Scottish Open skip.

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: Sudarshan Yellamaraju (model rank 1, 34 SG total) and Ryan Gerard (model rank 2, 94 SG total) are the two outright targets. Both carry the top-two model ranks and the largest model-to-power differentials in the supplied data.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: Sudarshan Yellamaraju, Ryan Gerard, and David Lipsky occupy the top-three model ranks and are the top-10 targets. Lipsky adds 524 SG around-the-green and 485 SG putting to complement the longer-game profile of the top two.

sections.heading: Top-20 Targets
sections.body: The same three players—Sudarshan Yellamaraju, Ryan Gerard, and David Lipsky—form the top-20 targets. Their model ranks of 1-2-3 and combined SG total of 34 / 94 / 89 supply the data backing.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are not available in this pipeline. The article does not make weather- or tee-time-specific claims.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Tier 1 (model-supported): Sudarshan Yellamaraju and Ryan Gerard for outright, top-5, top-10, and top-20. Tier 2 (model-supported): David Lipsky for top-10 and top-20.

article.conclusion: Sudarshan Yellamaraju (model rank 1) and Ryan Gerard (model rank 2) are the Tier-1 outright and top-5 targets. David Lipsky (model rank 3) joins them as a Tier-2 top-10 and top-20 play. All three carry zero tracked major-swing rounds and sit well ahead of their power ranks in the model.

Lipsky ranks third in the model at 0.89 SG total and 24th in power rank, posting 0.524 SG around-the-green and 0.485 SG putting.
All three targets carry zero tracked rounds in the major swing workload column and skipped the Scottish Open.
Course weights place 30% on SG total and 20% on SG approach, aligning with the top three model ranks' combined strength in those areas.
